newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- NOV 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- NOV 28.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--The state-run National Bank of Greece proceeds with a significant 0.5 percent reduction in interest rates on deposits as of today. The Ioanian Bank is expected to follow suit on Monday, while the Credit Bank is also expected to make changes to its deposit and lending rates.

--Tax breaks for journalists, MPs, public servants and airline pilots will continue to apply for 1996 incomes and will be abolished next year, according to the bill to be submitted to Parliament tomorrow, sources say.

--The Federation of Greek Industries (SEB) says austerity is a myth, noting that real increases in Greece in the last three years have increased at a greater rate than those in the European Union and the United States.
IMERISIA

--The market has greeted the government's new economic measures with shock, with SEB and business circles saying that they are disincentives for investment. Unionists, meanwhile, stage a general strike today.

--The European Investment Bank and the state will sign the Stavros-Elefsina road junction contract on December 16. A final decision on funding approval for the Rio-Antirrio bridge is expected on the 10th.
KERDOS

--The government is unwilling to back down on its economic measures in the face of a today's general strike. National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou however appears to enjoy the confidence of the prime minister.
--The real estate tax will be paid in three bi-monthly instalments, Deputy Finance Minister George Drys clarifies yesterday.
--SEB opposes further taxation of SMEs but in favour of abolition of tax breaks which have no development or social purpose.
--November inflation will fall to 7.9 percent and Greece will meet convergence targets by the end of 1998, Papandoniou told television viewers last night.

--The Capital Market Commission has introduced a new guideline allowing uncovered transactions up to the level of the firm's own capital; if trading exceeds own capital, the excess must be covered 100 percent.
EXPRESS
--The market judges Papandoniou's measures as well-intentioned but simply not enough. The main focus, they say, should fall on cutting back public expenditures.
--The finance ministry's new taxation legislation - to be submitted to Parliament along with the budget tomorrow - is particularly austere.
--The bourse's guarantee fund has filed suit against 10 persons and firms regarding the Delta Securities 2.6 billion drachma default two weeeks ago.
NAFTEMBORIKI

--Public transport grinds to a halt today as taxi drivers decide to join the General Confederation of Workers of Greece (GSEE) general strike. The restrictions on private vehicles in the city centre are lifted.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
